ABOUT KABIRA

A school built around
how children grow.

Kabira The International School is a preschool and daycare in Zirakpur, offering Pre-Nursery, Nursery, LKG, UKG and daycare, run by Bhattacharya Educational Trust. Kabira exists for a simple reason: young children deserve a place where they are known, not just enrolled.

As a new school, Kabira brings together a calm, welcoming environment with educational leadership shaped by nearly three decades in early childhood teaching, school administration and education management.

OUR BELIEF ABOUT EARLY CHILDHOOD

The early years
are the learning.

We believe the early years are not preparation for learning — they are learning. A child who feels safe enough to ask a question, try again after a mistake, or make a new friend is already building the confidence they will carry into every classroom that follows. That belief shapes how a school day is paced and how closely we work with parents.

OUR VISION

A personal school,
not a big one.

Our vision is simple: to give families in Zirakpur a preschool that feels personal — where academics grow alongside kindness and confidence, and where a strong beginning is treated as seriously as any exam. As Kabira grows, our hope is to walk with these same children into their primary years, in step with enrolment, infrastructure and the approvals such growth would require.

OUR VALUES

Kabir's Corner.

Inspired by Sant Kabir's wisdom, we treat good manners, discipline and respect as seriously as we treat phonics and numbers. These values rarely arrive through a lesson — they show up in returning a borrowed crayon, greeting a teacher, or waiting a turn at the story corner, and we treat those small moments as real teaching.

Kabir's Corner

Kindness · Honesty · Sharing · Gratitude · Respect

Small values, practised every day.

LEADERSHIP

A beginning you
can believe in.

Nearly 28 years in education have shaped Dr. Rita Rattan’s belief that a happy childhood begins with feeling understood. Her experience brings together preschool leadership, classroom teaching, school administration and years of listening to parents.

That experience shows up in how Kabira is run day to day: a settling-in period that isn't rushed, a teacher who notices when a child needs a quiet corner instead of a group activity, and everyday decisions made with a child's development in mind rather than convenience.

For parents, it means a Principal who is easy to reach, who has sat across from families making this decision many times before, and who treats a child's first days at school as seriously as any parent does.

“Every child needs to feel loved and understood before meaningful learning can begin.”

WHAT THAT EXPERIENCE MEANS FOR KABIRA

01

Child-centred decisions

Years spent in the classroom and at the admissions desk shape a habit of thinking about each decision from a child's point of view first.

02

Steady school management

Experience leading teams and running a centre day-to-day brings organisation and calm to how Kabira is managed.

03

Open, honest communication

A career spent talking with parents means questions are welcomed, not deflected — before, during and after admission.

Parents are part
of the conversation.

Dr. Rattan’s experience includes parent-teacher meetings, school events and daily coordination between families and staff. With English, Hindi and Punjabi among the languages she speaks, the aim is simple: clear conversations and a child who feels supported at school and at home.
